item.title: Full-Body Training Without Equipment: The Six Fundamental Movements You Need Every Week
item.description: Push, pull, squat, hinge, core, endurance — cover these six patterns and your training is complete. Why the model comes from movement science, how to apply it without a gym, and what a balanced week looks like.

item.title: HIIT or Zone 2? Which Cardio Actually Makes You Healthier
item.description: Intervals or easy steady-state training — the debate is old, but the answer is both. What VO₂max says about your life expectancy, what happens in your muscles during Zone 2, why HIIT is so efficient, and how to fit both into one week.

item.title: Learning Pull-Ups: From Zero to Your First Rep in Five Stages
item.description: The pull-up is the king exercise for back, arms, and grip strength — and initially out of reach for most beginners. Anatomy, why it is so hard, the five progression stages, and an 8-week roadmap.

item.title: How to Squat With Proper Form: Depth, Knee Angle, and the Myths Holding You Back
item.description: The squat is the most important exercise for legs, hips, and daily life in old age. Anatomy, what the research says about depth and "knees over toes," the most common mistakes, and a progression from the chair squat to single-leg variations — no equipment needed.

item.title: Core Training Done Right: Why Plank and Dead Bug Beat 100 Sit-Ups
item.description: The core is not a six-pack, it is a stabilization system. What spine research says about sit-ups, the four jobs of the core, Stuart McGill's "Big Three," and a progression from your first plank second to the hollow hold.

item.title: Sleep and Recovery: Why Your Progress Happens Between Workouts
item.description: Training is the stimulus, recovery is the adaptation. What sleep deprivation does to muscle growth, strength, and injury risk, how supercompensation works, how to spot overtraining, and a recovery protocol for athletes with a real life.

item.title: The History of the Push-Up: From Wrestling Schools to the World Record
item.description: Who invented the push-up? A journey from Indian wrestling schools through the German gymnastics movement and 20th-century military tests to 46,001 reps in 24 hours and the 2019 Harvard study.

item.title: Pain During Push-Ups: Protecting Your Wrists, Shoulders, and Elbows
item.description: Wrist, shoulder, elbow, or lower back — almost every push-up pain has a mechanical cause. Anatomy, the most common triggers, a pain traffic-light, and a 10-minute prehab routine.

item.title: Building Muscle With Push-Ups: What the Research Really Says About Bodyweight Training
item.description: Can you build muscle without dumbbells? Yes — under three conditions. The studies comparing push-ups to bench press, the rep-range continuum, and a concrete plan for progressive overload without any weights.

item.title: Which Muscles Do Push-Ups Train? Anatomy, EMG Data, and Hand Positions
item.description: Chest, triceps, shoulders — and half a dozen silent helpers. What the research actually knows about muscle activation, moved bodyweight, and hand positions during push-ups.

item.title: The 7 most common push-up mistakes — and how to fix each one
item.description: Bad form costs you reps, progress, and sometimes your shoulder. The most common push-up mistakes, with concrete fixes for each.

item.title: Push-ups for women: myths, anatomy, and a 4-week starting plan
item.description: Women can do the same push-ups as men — the progression often just looks different. Anatomy, myths, and a realistic 4-week starter plan.

item.title: Breathing for push-ups: bracing, rhythm, and what changes at max effort
item.description: Breathing is undersold for push-ups. When to inhale, when to exhale, what bracing means — and why max-effort sets need a different rule.

item.title: The Harvard Study That Made Push-Ups Famous: 40+ Reps and Heart Health
item.description: A 2019 JAMA study put push-up capacity on the cardiovascular-risk map. Here is what the data actually said, what it did not, and how to use it for your own training.

item.title: The Wim Hof Method for Push-Ups: Breathing, Cold Exposure & Performance
item.description: Can the Wim Hof Method really boost push-up performance and recovery? A research-based look at the breathing protocol, cold exposure, and what the evidence actually shows.

item.title: Push-Ups After 40: How to Train Safely and Effectively
item.description: Your body changes after 40 – but push-ups remain one of the best exercises. Learn how to build strength safely with the right adjustments.

item.title: 30-Day Push-Up Challenge: Your Plan for Maximum Progress
item.description: This structured 30-day challenge helps you increase your push-up count step by step – from week 1 to the final test on day 30.

item.title: 10 Push-Up Variations for Every Fitness Level
item.description: From knee push-ups to archer push-ups: these 10 variations target chest, triceps, and shoulders – and break through any plateau.

item.title: How a Tracker Helps You Hit Push-Up Personal Bests
item.description: Why a digital push-up tracker makes the difference – and how Pushup Tracker helps you achieve personal bests and stay consistent.

item.title: Why Daily Push-Ups Will Change Your Life
item.description: Daily push-ups improve strength, posture, and well-being. Discover the scientifically proven benefits and how to build the habit for good.
